Equal observed lengths are not a veto. Qualified KEY and LOCATOR syntax retain precedence; fixed contents remain literal.

established_wording_key_run_loss.authority: Engineering correction under owner instructions to preserve independently established diagnostic wording while excluding supported KEY values from comparison. The owner did not prescribe this algorithm or threshold. v39 native validation exposed loss of a single word from established runs, which the former adjacent-KEY-only check missed.
established_wording_key_run_loss.mechanic: Reject a proposed merge when any complete word in a previously literal run of at least two alphabetic raw tokens would become KEY/OPTIONAL_KEY content. The previous template must already have at least two distinct values in a non-LOCATOR field. Inspect only previous literals, never words inside accepted captures. Raw punctuation, fields and line endings interrupt a run. Isolated old spellings remain eligible for field discovery. This is a conservative merge-evidence check, not default literals, vocabulary classification or an initial slot grammar; it can retain narrower templates for unquoted identifiers embedded in established wording. Two words is the minimum run length, evaluated on complete native logs.

field_similarity.authority: Owner 2026-09-27 reiterates that a corresponding field at the correct position counts once, like one matching token, irrespective of its contents. Slot contents must not contribute individual word matches or become diagnostic wording.
field_similarity.mechanic: Retain ordered literal-word units and one typed unit per recognized present field. Declared fields participate from recognition; inferred fields participate only after complete capture validation. Hypothesized unaccepted regions receive no field credit. slot_position_cues.authority: Owner requires file/line labels outside LOCATOR captures and no forced numeric conversion for identifier fields. The existing regexes are implementation heuristics, not owner-prescribed regex syntax or new example-specific typing rules. Owner 2026-09-21: the value following Database: in Key <KEY> not found at Database: is a LOCATOR; its label remains literal. Owner follow-up: recognized locations must remain LOCATOR, not literal wording, even when observations share one path spelling, including words within paths. Recognition uses known labels and complete parser tokens; never colon-to-line-end masking.
slot_position_cues.filename_authority: Owner: .txt, .yml, .md and .py establish filename evidence without a directory separator. These explicit examples are suffix cues, not a folder whitelist or a claim that every dotted CK3 key is a filename. Other extensions can be recognized in path/file contexts or filename:line notation. Explicit file context bounds names containing spaces; do not join spaced slash lists without location context.
slot_position_cues.line_suffix_authority: Owner: file.txt:6 is filename, colon punctuation, line reference. The path and line are separate LOCATOR fields with the colon literal between them. Native GUI .gui:number and dynasty .txt:number forms support the generic boundary; existing scope:key and dotted identifiers remain intact.
slot_position_cues.path_value_authority: Owner: recognize slash-delimited path formulations after a colon, file, or in using syntax and complete ranges of adjacent raw segment and slash tokens, including unfamiliar or mod-created paths. No folder allowlist, required extension, or required :number suffix for these contextual forms. Numeric ratios alone are not path evidence. Slash-delimited filename syntax with an extension also supplies evidence without those introducers. Slash is a separate punctuation token, not internal identifier punctuation. Preserve native attached location suffixes when present, separately labelled line fields, and surrounding wording; do not swallow subsequent trace content. Regex implementation is a reviewable lexical heuristic, not an owner-specified regex.

publication.authority: Owner-authorized model delivery. This export preserves the reviewed candidate templates, statuses, JSON-declared policy and complete assignment interface. Publication alone does not activate the pipeline or change its selection.
